🧪 Data Validation & Integrity Checks

Before model training, rigorous validation tests are performed to ensure data quality and consistency. Class Balance checks for distribution shifts between training and testing sets, which is critical for generalization. Feature Scaling ensures all inputs are normalized (typically [-1, 1] or [0, 1]) to prevent gradient explosion/vanishing in neural networks. Dimensionality Consistency verifies that input shapes match the model's expected architecture.

Test Details Status

🏆 Main Model Comparison (with Best GLU)

This section compares the performance of baseline models (MLP, LSTM, CNN) against the best-performing CNN-GLU variant. Accuracy measures overall correctness. Precision indicates the quality of positive predictions (few false positives). Recall (Sensitivity) measures the ability to find all positive instances (few false negatives). F1 Score is the harmonic mean of Precision and Recall, providing a single metric for balanced performance.

🔄 Cross-Validation Analysis (Best Model)

K-Fold Cross-Validation (k=5) provides a robust estimate of model performance by training on different subsets of the data. Unlike a single train-test split, CV reduces variance in performance estimation and highlights if the model is overfitting to a specific data subset. The comparison below shows how the model's stability (CV Mean) compares to its performance on the hold-out Test Set.

📉 Prediction Probability Distribution

This histogram visualizes the model's confidence in its predictions. A strong model separates the Positive Class (Target) and Negative Class probabilities into distinct clusters (near 1.0 and 0.0 respectively). Overlapping regions indicate samples where the model is uncertain (decision boundary ambiguity).

🔬 GLU Variants Comparison

Gated Linear Units (GLU) allow the network to control information flow, potentially mitigating the vanishing gradient problem. We compare different GLU activation functions (e.g., Sigmoid, Tanh, ReLU) to identify which gating mechanism best captures the dataset's underlying patterns.

🧩 Confusion Matrices

The Confusion Matrix provides a detailed breakdown of prediction errors. Diagonal elements represent correct predictions (True Negatives, True Positives). Off-diagonal elements represent errors (False Positives, False Negatives). A high concentration of values on the diagonal indicates a robust model.

Feature Importance Magnitude

Interpretation: comparison of feature importance on Train vs. Test data.

🌊 Predicted Probability Density Maps

Interpretation: These density plots show the distribution of predicted probabilities for each model on the Test Set.

  • Goal: A good model should separate the two classes distinctly.
  • Positive Class (Blue): Should have a peak near 1.0.
  • Negative Class (Red): Should have a peak near 0.0.
  • Overlap: Intersection area represents model uncertainty/confusion.

🔄 Cross-Validation vs. Independent Test ROC

Interpretation: This graph compares the Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) curves from the 5-Fold Cross-Validation (training phase) against the final Independent Test Set.

  • Robustness Check: If the Test ROC (Bold Line) lies within or close to the CV folds (Faint Lines), the model is robust and not overfitting.
  • Performance Gap: A significant drop in the Test ROC compared to CV suggests the model might not generalize well to unseen data.
  • AUC Stability: Consistent AUC scores across folds indicate stable training data distribution.
